1.why: All ten screenshots show a static, single-column layout with no animations, carousels, or pop-up dialogs — only static cards, banners and a log panel.

2.why: Each step has a bold dark-blue heading, a single prominent blue primary button and colour-coded info banners, though the large dark 'Recovery activity logs' block competes visually with the actual task card.

3.why: Only one task with one or two fields per screen and a clearly labelled primary action makes the next step easy to locate, but the technical token/log content adds noise for a non-technical user.

4.why: The flow is guided step-by-step, yet the user must carry a 64-character token and a six-digit code across screens and remember four password rules simultaneously.

5.why: No password manager hint, autofill affordance, 'remember me' checkbox, or show-password toggle appears on any screen, including the password creation step (steps 6–7).

6.why: The token is pre-filled on step 3 and the code is displayed on step 4, but nothing is presented as saved/familiar to the user — there is no account name, avatar, masked email echo or saved-item recognition.

7.why: Sentences are short, plain-language and in a readable sans-serif with good contrast, though the hex token string and console-style log text are dense and unreadable in meaning.

8.why: No error state is shown in any of the ten screenshots; only static advisory banners appear, so the claim that error messages describe problem and fix cannot be observed as true.

9.why: The MFA step shows the exact code to type (246810) and the password step lists concrete requirements, but no worked example password or email format example is given.

10.why: The flow is fixed to token + emailed code + password; there is no choice of authentication method (no code/face/passkey options presented anywhere).

11.why: Every screen presents at most two buttons and one or two inputs, so the user is never faced with many simultaneous choices.

12.why: Each action produces a confirmation banner and a timestamped log entry (e.g. 'Recovery token verified', 'Password reset completed', final 'Recovery complete'), though outcomes are partly conveyed via technical log text.

13.why: Short helper hints appear under fields and in the yellow banners plus a repeated 'Keep your account safe' block, but there is no contextual help link, tooltip or progress guidance for new steps.

14.why: Step 2 offers 'Start over' and step 10 offers 'Begin another recovery', but intermediate screens (3, 4, 6, 8) have no back, cancel or retry control visible.

15.why: Header, card layout, banner styling, button colours and the safety footer are identical across all ten steps, giving a highly consistent, learnable design.
